subject: Urgent: Sable Financial p99 latency spike after v4.1 q-profile rollout
messages:
From: María Gómez <maria.gomez@sablefin.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: platform@accounts.sablefin.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden p99 latency spike after v4.1 q-profile rollout

Diego —

We saw a sharp jump in p99 latency and a small but noticeable increase in error rate starting ~08:45 PST right after the v4.1 q-profile (QProfile-B) went live. The product team is seeing timeouts in our user-facing inference endpoint (tokenization+generate) and throughput for peak flows has dropped ~28%. Attached are side-by-side p99 traces for the last 24h and the 1h window showing the start of the spike.

This rollout was scheduled as a performance improvement; instead it's regressing latency for our high-concurrency workflows. We need immediate mitigation and an ETA for rollback if required. Our compliance window for the day means we can't accept prolonged tail latency.

What we expect: a quick mitigation plan (rollback or config fallback), a short postmortem, and note whether this will impact contract SLAs. Please escalate to product/infra and let us know next steps within 30 minutes if possible.

--
María Gómez
Director, Platform Engineering
Sable Financial
attachments: sable-p99-compare-11-18.pdf

Subject: Re: Sudden p99 latency spike after v4.1 q-profile rollout

María — thanks for the quick heads up and the traces. I see the same jump on our side in the telemetry and the increased 5xxs coincident with the q-profile flip.

Immediate actions I am initiating now:
- I have flagged this to our on-call runtime team and asked for an emergency canary rollback option for Sable only (target: next 30–45m).
- Karthik is copied for commercial/exec alignment; I'll coordinate the communications.
- Lauren — can you confirm whether QProfile-B included the new KV compression path we shipped? If so, we should try a qprofile revert + keep the model binary; if not, we should be able to toggle the runtime fallback to v4.0 behavioral path.

If we can't restore within the window, we will schedule an immediate single-tenant rollback for Sable to the previous qprofile and open a targeted incident bridge. I'll update in 20 minutes with telemetry and a recommended mitigation.

Diego
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sudden p99 latency spike after v4.1 q-profile rollout

Diego / team —

Quick update from runtime: QProfile-B enabled a new cache-compression codec (LZP-3) and a slightly more aggressive token batching heuristic for mid-sequence workloads. On our lab repro with Sable's workload trace, the compression path introduces a CPU serialization point that increases tail latency under high concurrency; combined with the batching heuristic it produces longer critical sections.

Plan A (fastest): rollback Sable to QProfile-A (previous profile) for their fleet. This is a config flip and should be safe; estimated time to full restore: 35–50 minutes. Runbook attached (rollback_runbook.md).

Plan B (if rollback fails): enable runtime fallback that disables the new compression codec while keeping other optimizations; this will reduce throughput modestly but recover p99.

I'll be on the bridge and will run the rollback if Diego signs off. I will also capture traces for a short postmortem and a perf/quality comparison pass.

Lauren
Principal Product Engineer — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
attachments: rollback_runbook.md, qprofile-change-log.csv

Subject: Re: Sudden p99 latency spike after v4.1 q-profile rollout — rollback completed and exec summary

María / Sable team —

Follow-up summary and next steps (post-rollback):

What happened
- On 2026-11-18 08:45 PST Sable's production fleet flipped to QProfile-B during the scheduled rollout window. Telemetry showed a rapid p99 increase and a rise in timeouts correlated with the new cache-compression path.

Immediate mitigation
- At 09:50 PST on 2026-11-18 we executed a targeted rollback to QProfile-A for Sable only. The rollback finished at 10:18 PST. p99 returned to baseline within two full garbage-collection intervals; throughput recovered to expected levels (~+30% from the spike nadir).

Lasting actions
- Engineering will pause further QProfile-B rollouts until we ship a patch that removes the serialization hotspot. We will run a controlled A/B with small traffic slices and extended tail monitoring.
- We will provide Sable with daily telemetry exports for 72 hours and a short postmortem that includes the perf diff and candidate fixes.
- Commercial: Karthik will follow up on SLA credits and executive notes; we will prepare a customer-facing incident timeline.

Attachments included: sable-p99-compare-11-18.pdf, rollback_runbook.md, qprofile-change-log.csv

Apologies for the disruption — we understand the impact and will prioritize the fix. Karthik will coordinate exec comms.

Diego Fernandez
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
